 Live .  13,406 viewing 13406 viewing Live page Updated 3 minutes ago Legendary Star Trek actor Sir Patrick Stewart dies aged 86
 Summary
 Legendary Star Trek actor Sir Patrick Stewart has died aged 86 
 His co-stars have led tributes, with William Shatner saying that Stewart "stood for the best of us" 
 Meanwhile, actor Hugh Jackman says "we lost one of the greats of stage and screen" 
 The Royal Shakespeare Company describes the actor as a "colossus" and flowers are due to be placed on his star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame 
 Stewart died at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday , according to a statement shared on his social media
 The award-winning star had a career across decades - from the Shakespearean stage, to the X-Men franchise 
 His appeal crossed generations, and younger fans will have discovered his work on streaming platforms, writes our culture correspondent Noor Nanji 
 Media caption, Sir Patrick Stewart: The life of a legendary actor Live Reporting
 Edited by Brajesh Upadhyay, with reporting from culture correspondent Noor Nanji
 Former co-star Dame Harriet Walter 'can't imagine a world without him' published at 23:30 GMT 23:30 GMT 
 Newsnight 
 Image source, Press Association The actress Dame Harriet Walter - who knew Sir Patrick Stewart for more than 40 years - has told BBC Newsnight "the world's going to be very poor without him".
 "It's like huge giant tree has fallen in the forest. I can't really imagine a world without him," she said. 
 Dame Harriet first met Sir Patrick at Stratford-upon-Avon in the early 1980s, and later played Cleopatra alongside his Antony in 2006.
 Recalling his acting, she told Newsnight: "The man was alive in the moment. And that's my favourite kind of acting. He never got set into habits. He was always just alive."
 "He had fire in his eyes and you were absolutely in the room with him," added Dame Harriet, who more recently has appeared in series Ted Lasso and Succession.
 "I've never heard a bad word against him. And I think the world's going to be very poor without him."

 'A heartbreaking reminder of the devastating impact dementia has,' says charity head published at 23:18 GMT 23:18 GMT 
 Noor Nanji 
Culture correspondent 
 As we've been reporting, Patrick Stewart died at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday after suffering with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
 Now, we've had a tribute from Alzheimer's Society.
 Writing on X, their CEO Michelle Dyson called Stewart "an extraordinarily talented and much-loved actor, admired by millions around the world".
 “His death is a heartbreaking reminder of the devastating impact dementia has on people and families across the globe," she said.
 She reminded readers that Alzheimer’s Society is "here for everyone affected by dementia".

 'A captain unlike any other': Star Trek celebrates life of Patrick Stewart published at 23:02 GMT 23:02 GMT 
 Image source, CBS via Getty Images The official Star Trek social media account has thanked Patrick Stewart, who played Captain Jean-Luc Picard, following his death.
 "A voice. A presence. A captain unlike any other," the account says.
 It adds: "Sir Patrick Stewart gave generations of fans an icon who inspired us to look toward the stars. Today, we celebrate an extraordinary life and an enduring legacy."
 Stewart played Picard in over 170 episodes of the sci-fi television series between 1987 and 1994, and in four feature films before returning in Star Trek: Picard from 2020 to 2023.

 Flowers have already been laid on Stewart's Hollywood star published at 22:49 GMT 22:49 GMT 
 Regan Morris 
Reporting from Los Angeles 
 Image source, Regan Morris Media are gathered at Patrick Stewart’s star on the Walk of Fame awaiting the official laying of flowers. 
 Stewart’s star on Hollywood Boulevard has been there since 16 December 1996. The Walk of Fame plans to place flowers on his star at 4 pm local time (2300g).
 But a local florist has already left some flowers and someone else left a rose and a card.

 A clip from 30 years ago shows Patrick Stewart on the day he received his Hollywood Walk of Fame star, saying he was "delighted".

 A life on stage and screen published at 22:29 GMT 22:29 GMT 
 In a career that spanned six decades, Stewart received multiple awards, a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame and a knighthood from Queen Elizabeth II.
 1966 : His first professional foray into acting was at the Royal Shakespeare Company, which he joined after winning a scholarship to the Bristol Old Vic
 1967 : He made his TV debut as a fireman on an episode of the soap opera Coronation street
 1987 : After a string of television roles over two decades, his breakthrough role came when he played Captain Jean-Luc Picard in the Star Trek series and subsequent films
 2000 : Stewart was cast as Professor X in the X-men franchise alongside actor Sir Ian McKellen
 2009 : He returned to the stage alongside McKellen in the play Waiting for Godot

 Legendary Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86 published at 22:22 GMT 22:22 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images If you’re just joining us, we’re continuing to bring you the latest on legendary Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart, who died on Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles. He was 86.
 The actor was suffering with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, his Instagram account announced on Thursday.
 Known for his roles in Star Trek, X-Men and the Royal Shakespeare Company, Stewart had a career spanning six decades.
 Tributes have been pouring in since the news broke, with X-Men co-star Hugh Jackman remembering Stewart as “one of the greats”.

 Star Trek co-star Wil Wheaton speaks on 'gravitas' Stewart brought to programme published at 22:11 GMT 22:11 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Wil Wheaton, who starred alongside Stewart in Star Trek: The Next Generation, has said the late actor brought "a wonderful kind of tone" to the cast.
 Speaking to BBC Radio 4's the World Tonight programme, the actor who played Wesley Crusher says: "Patrick, like the rest of the cast of Star Trek: The Next Generation, treated me with more love, more unconditional love, more support, and more kindness than my parents."
 Wheaton says Stewart brought "gravitas" to the programme, bringing it a level of respectability and intensity from spending time in the Royal Shakespeare Company.
 Describing the loss as "very profound", he says: "He always made me feel so special when we were in scenes together. He made me a better actor just by being there. He was so kind, and so generous and gentle with me specifically."

 'A colossus of both stage and screen', says Royal Shakespeare Company published at 22:00 GMT 22:00 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Stewart alongside David Tennant during a production of Hamlet in 2008 with the Royal Shakespeare Company
 The Royal Shakespeare Company has described the late Patrick Stewart as "a colossus of both stage and screen".
 Remembering him as "one of the finest classical Shakespearean actors of his generation", the company says his contribution to it is "beyond measure".
 He says: "Despite being one of the most recognisable Shakespearean performers in the world, Sir Patrick remained deeply connected to Stratford-upon-Avon and the RSC throughout his career."

 Advocacy group honours 'true giant for animal welfare' published at 21:49 GMT 21:49 GMT 
 Noor Nanji 
Culture correspondent 
 Away from his stage and screen work, Patrick Stewart was a huge animal lover and fostered pit bulls.
 This evening, the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (RSPCA) are among those paying tribute to him.
 "Icons like Captain Picard and Professor X defined his screen legacy, but Sir Patrick was also a true giant for animal welfare, and we are proud to have campaigned alongside him to make this a kinder world," says Thomas Schultz-Jagow, Executive Director of Advocacy and Prevention at the RSPCA. 
 "In particular, Sir Patrick used his iconic voice to champion every dog - regardless of their breed. 
 "His kindness, compassion and advocacy will be sorely missed."
 Image source, Getty Images

 Stewart's Hollywood Walk of Fame star to receive flower tributes published at 21:35 GMT 21:35 GMT 
 Regan Morris 
Reporting from Los Angeles 
 Image source, Getty Images Flowers will be placed on Patrick Stewart’s star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame today to pay tribute to the late actor. 
 Stewart’s star on Hollywood Boulevard has been there since 16 December 1996. The Walk of Fame plans to place flowers on his star at 4 pm local time (2300g) 
 “With heavy hearts, we will place flowers on Sir Patrick Stewart’s Hollywood Walk of Fame star in honour of a remarkable talent whose legacy touched millions,” Ana Martinez of the Hollywood Walk of Fame said in a statement. 
 "It was our privilege to pay tribute to an extraordinary artist who will never be forgotten. Rest in peace, Sir Patrick.”

 Stewart's death comes days after another Star Trek actor died published at 21:25 GMT 21:25 GMT 
 Stewart's death comes in the same week as that of another Star Trek actor. 
 Walter Koenig, who played the spirited Russian crewman Pavel Chekov in the original Star Trek TV series, died aged 90.
 The pair worked together on the 1994 film, Star Trek Generations.
 Image source, CBS via Getty Images.

 Stewart's talent was clear before he broke through as an actor published at 21:16 GMT 21:16 GMT 
 The son of a textile worker mother and a father who was a regimental sergeant major in the British army, Patrick Stewart began his career performing in amateur dramatics in his home town of Mirfield, as well as alongside Brian Blessed in Calder Valley summer theatre workshops.
 His talent as a teenager was clear, according to a local newspaper account - on display at the exhibition - of his last performance before he left for Bristol in 1957 when he was 17.
 "As has now come to be expected, he played his part with considerable ease and was clearly audible," wrote the Mirfield Reporter's theatre critic in a lukewarm review of the local drama club's production of Ronald Jeans' comedy Young Wives' Tale.
 Despite the initial rejections after leaving theatre school, work was soon flowing Sir Patrick's way.
 He landed his first professional role playing Tom Morgan in Treasure Island at Lincoln's Theatre Royal in 1959 before working at the Sheffield Playhouse for 18 months.

 The stage as an 'escape' for Sir Patrick published at 21:08 GMT 21:08 GMT 
 Noor Nanji 
Culture correspondent 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Patrick Stewart appeared in Waiting For Godot alongside Ian McKellen in 2009.
 Patrick Stewart had a long and hugely successful career. 
 It was at school where his love of drama developed, when one of his teachers introduced him to Shakespeare and encouraged him to perform.
 His first public performance was in a local church production of Cinderella. Speaking many years later to the Guardian, he said that he realised early that on stage, he could "escape".
 "And my dream became more of a dream. Not just of having a different life. But, for the few minutes I had on stage, actually living it.”

 Stewart 'inspired a generation of star-gazers' - Star Trek co-star George Takei published at 21:00 GMT 21:00 GMT 
 Emma Saunders 
Culture reporter 
 Image source, Getty Images George Takei, who played Mr Sulu in Star Trek, has also paid tribute to his former co-star.
 "Fans across the world mourn the passing of a true and irreplaceable legend," he writes on Instagram. 
 "As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Patrick Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before, and he inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity."
 "Our hearts are heavy, indeed. Rest in the heavens, Captain."

 Stewart is survived by wife and two children published at 20:52 GMT 20:52 GMT 
 Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Patrick Stewart and his wife Sunny Ozell
 The veteran actor is survived by his wife Sunny Ozell , who was with him when he passed away at home according to a statement sent to the BBC by his spokesperson.
 He is also survived by two adult children from his first marriage: Daniel Stewart and Sophie Stewart. 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Daniel Stewart and Patrick Stewart in 2015

 Speaking in 2011, Patrick Stewart recalls when he was told he would "never be a leading man" and how he broke through into acting in the first place.

 X-Men co-star Hugh Jackman remembers 'one of the greats' published at 20:46 GMT 20:46 GMT Breaking 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Hugh Jackman and Patrick Stewart, pictured at a press event in March 2017
 Hugh Jackman has paid tribute to his former X-Men co-star, describing Sir Patrick Stewart as a "tremendous friend and man".
 The actor says in a post on Instagram: "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today."
 "I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days," he adds.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Captain Picard stood for the best of us,' says Star Trek co-star William Shatner published at 20:45 GMT 20:45 GMT Breaking 
 Image source, Getty Images William Shatner, who portrayed Captain Kirk on Star Trek, remembers his former co-star as "a magnificent colleague".
 "What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," he says. 
 "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did.
 "Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work.
 "My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed."
